notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/quantumllama__python-lab-drivers --backend fake; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: none. The card's family-config/ScpiDriver fits the clone's plain command lines, and native is the card's first entry symbol func_gen_test:func_gen (a module-level PyVISA resource variable; the clone has no class). The card lists two override entry symbols; this package serves the first, the Siglent SDG 2042X function generator. The second, oscope_test:oscope, is NOT COVERED: its whole interface in the clone is *IDN? plus MENU ON/MENU OFF (oscope_test.py:19-23), so it is not a second device of this package.

Covered: output state (C2:OUTP?), waveform, frequency, peak-to-peak amplitude, DC offset and duty cycle (C2:BaSic_WaVe?), each also writable through the bridge's cap.device.configure.v1 using the long command spellings of func_gen_test.py:22-25. The e-stop writes C2:OUTP OFF, disabling the generator output. The frequency, amplitude and offset ranges are Limit.operator_required because the programming guide gives the units and refers the range of valid values to the data sheet, which is not in the clone; without a site-limits.json those three writes are refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. Duty cycle is limited to 0..100 percent and the waveform to the eight WVTP values, both sourced from the PDF guide page 20; the output states ON/OFF are sourced from func_gen_test.py:22-25. site-limits.example.json only narrows duty_cycle to at most 50 percent and the waveform to SQUARE; it deliberately does not invent ranges for the operator-required fields.

The upstream clone has no simulator and no recorded session, so fake.py is an in-memory SCPI transport stand-in, not a recording; every starting value and canned reply is marked # placeholder in fake.py and is test data, never a Fact or a Limit. fixtures/conformance.json supplies duty_cycle 40/41 as the valid/alternate configure inputs because the conformance synthesis otherwise chooses an operator-required field (amplitude) and stops at LIMITS_UNSET; it also carries out-of-envelope duty, output and waveform inputs. The fake answers only the commands the driver sends, and those command tokens all occur in the clone.

G4 reports seven REF_BINARY warnings because the clone supplies the vendor text only as SDG_Wavegen_Programming_Guide.pdf and the gate cannot read a PDF page. They cannot be cleared without inventing a bound: two Limits (waveform and duty_cycle) and five Facts cite physical pages 14 (the *IDN? response format), 19 (the output command), 20 (waveform list and duty range) and 20-21 (the basic-wave command and query form). A reviewer opens those pages. No G4.REF_VALUE warning was reported.

The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); the hardware backend was never started and nothing here ran on an instrument. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest the last check printed.
